text:
Jake Evans, a seventh-round pick who has spent his whole career in Montreal, has become one of the Canadiens' most useful forwards with half the top six hurt. He has moved into Ivan Demidov's spot beside Juraj Slafkovský and Alex Newhook, and he has four goals and ten points in 24 games, his goals right in line with his chances. Montreal takes 53% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on (expected goals measure the quality of chances), almost four points better than without him.

The team has scored about four more goals than its chances with him out there, so his points are a little padded. Still, a depth center tilting the ice is a step up from last season, when Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level. He also has the number Dylan Larkin wore in Detroit, and Larkin said he has too much respect for Evans to ask for 71, per The Hockey News. With Larkin arriving, watch where Evans ends up in the lineup.
